skill.name: spec-driven-development
skill.description: Guides AI-assisted development through a seven-phase Spec-Driven Development workflow with constitution, specification, clarification, planning, analysis, task breakdown, and implementation phases.
skill.summary: Run a governed Spec-Driven Development workflow from project principles to validated implementation tasks.
skill.author: Joseph OBrien

content.value_statement: Complex AI-assisted projects can lose clarity before implementation starts. This skill guides teams through phased specifications, governance, planning, analysis, and task execution.
actual_capabilities: Defines a seven-phase workflow from project constitution to implementation.
Guides creation of specifications, plans, research notes, data models, and task lists.
Uses quality gates for clarifications, analysis, and constitution alignment.
Explains task dependencies, user story grouping, and optional parallel work markers.
Describes coordination patterns for Claude, Codex, Claude Code, and other coding agents.
limitations: It provides methodology guidance, not executable automation.
It does not include the referenced scripts or templates as files.
Users must adapt artifacts to their project stack and team rules.
Security, compliance, and architecture decisions still require human review.

use_cases.title: Turn Feature Ideas Into Requirements
use_cases.description: Create stakeholder-focused specifications with scenarios, acceptance criteria, edge cases, and measurable success criteria.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Parallel Delivery
use_cases.description: Break planned work into dependency-aware tasks that multiple developers or AI agents can execute with clear handoffs.

use_cases.title: Prepare AI Coding Sessions
use_cases.description: Move from clarified goals to implementation-ready tasks before asking an AI coding assistant to modify files.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Feature Specification
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for turning an idea into a structured specification.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use spec-driven-development to create a stakeholder-focused specification for [feature]. Ask clarification questions before planning.

prompt_templates.title: Clarify Missing Requirements
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for resolving ambiguity before planning work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my specification for [feature]. Identify the highest-impact ambiguities and ask one question at a time.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Implementation Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for turning a clarified specification into a technical plan.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the SDD planning phase for [feature]. Produce the technical context, research needs, design artifacts, and quality gates.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Multi-Agent Execution
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for dividing work across people or AI coding agents.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a dependency-ordered task breakdown for [feature]. Mark independent tasks and define handoff points for multiple agents.

output_examples.input: A team wants to build account recovery but only has a rough feature idea.
output_examples.output: A structured feature specification with user scenarios, acceptance criteria, edge cases, functional requirements, and success criteria.

output_examples.input: An engineering lead needs several agents to work on one feature safely.
output_examples.output: A task plan grouped by user story, with dependencies, foundational work, validation steps, and parallel work markers.

output_examples.input: A project has specs, plans, and tasks that may not agree.
output_examples.output: A severity-ranked analysis report covering duplications, ambiguities, underspecified items, and constitution conflicts.

best_practices: Establish the constitution before creating feature plans or implementation tasks.
Resolve high-impact clarification questions before selecting technologies or writing tasks.
Run analysis before implementation to catch inconsistencies across specs, plans, and tasks.
anti_patterns: Starting implementation before the specification has clear acceptance criteria.
Creating parallel tasks without explicit dependencies and handoff points.
Treating the methodology as a substitute for security, compliance, or architecture review.

faq.question: Does this skill write code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides a methodology for preparing specifications, plans, analysis, and task breakdowns.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow describes agent-neutral artifacts that can guide several AI coding tools.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when a feature needs clear requirements, governance, planning, and implementation sequencing before coding starts.

faq.question: Does it require GitHub SpecKit to be installed?
faq.answer: No. The skill explains a SpecKit-inspired workflow, but this package only contains documentation.

faq.question: Is it useful for small prototypes?
faq.answer: Yes. Use a lighter version with focused specifications, fewer planning artifacts, and small user stories.

faq.question: What should users review manually?
faq.answer: Users should review security requirements, compliance constraints, architecture choices, and any generated implementation tasks.
